newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER ROARS ON BACK NINE, TAKES THREE-SHOT MASTERS LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER ROARS ON BACK NINE, TAKES THREE-SHOT MASTERS LEAD.

text.p: Tiger Woods roared through the back nine at Augusta National on Friday to seize a startling three-stroke lead over Briton Colin Montgomerie after the second round of the Masters.
Woods used an eagle-three at the par-five 13th to launch his charge, overtaking Montgomerie at that point and then adding birdies on the next two holes to finish with a spectacular six-under-par 66.
The 21-year-old Woods, shooting to become the youngest ever winner of the Masters, stood at eight-under-par 136.
"I felt very relaxed today. I was very patient today," said Woods, playing his third Masters but first as a professional.
"My strategy is to drive the par-fives well. If I do, I can reach them all pretty easily in two and should be able to score at least a four."
The exceptionally long-hitting Woods played the four par-fives in five under par on Friday.

Montgomerie, the European tour's leading money winner the last four seasons, finished the day alone in second place at 139 after a sparkling five-under-par round of 67 that featured seven birdies against two bogeys.
The Briton's second bogey of the day, at the par-three 16th, dropped him to five under par and out of the lead as it coincided with Woods's eagle for a three-stroke swing.
Italian Costantino Rocca, Montgomerie's Ryder Cup teammate, turned in a three-under-par round of 69 to hold third place at four-under-par 140.
Former Masters champions Jose Maria Olazabal of Spain and Fred Couples were tied at three-under 141, five strokes behind Woods, along with former PGA champion Jeff Sluman.
Only seven players broke par Thursday in brutal conditions when wind and fiendish pin placements combined to make Augusta National's racetrack-fast greens look fit for Formula One.
Gentler breezes and fairer pin placements greeted the players Friday and the scramble was on in a crowded leaderboard.
"The course was at least three shots easier today," said Montgomerie.

Montgomerie has challenged in both the U.S. Open and in the PGA Championship, losing both in playoffs, but has not found any success yet at the Masters. The burly Briton, who will be paired Saturday with Woods, was not making any predictions.
"It all depends on Mr Woods," he said. "This course suits him better than the rest of us, so we'll just have to see.
"He's playing his ball and I'm playing mine. On the drives, I wish I was playing his."
Six strokes off the pace at two-under-par 142 were Nick Price of Zimbabwe, Paul Azinger and Paul Stankowski.
Nineteen players broke par on Friday but some notables were unable to take advantage.
Two players were embarrassed at the same par-five 13th that Woods used as a springboard to the lead.
John Huston, the first-round leader after a five-under 67, was jockeying with the others at the top of the leaderboard until he came to unlucky 13.

Huston recorded an astounding 10 on the 13th, twice landing in the water guarding the green and barely staying dry above the creek a third time, as he soared from four-under to one-over on the hole. He finished with a 77 for 144.
Defending champion Nick Faldo also came undone at 13. After laying up short of the par-five's green, the Briton splashed wedge shots twice on his way to a nine.

Faldo, a three-time Masters champion, finished the day with a mind-boggling 81 -- his worst score in 60 major championships. Combined with his opening 75, the Briton missed his first Masters cut with a woeful 156 total.
Faldo declined to answer questions about his round. "Sorry, no. I'm kind of flabbergasted," he said.

Greg Norman, runner-up to Faldo last year after a last-round collapse, added a 74 to his opening 77 for 151 and snapped his streak of 14 consecutive cuts made in the majors -- the longest active streak.
"It was just one of those things," said Norman. "It wasn't my week."
The cut was established at five-over-par 149, allowing 46 players to compete over the weekend.
Other well-known players to miss the cut included Phil Mickelson (150), last week's tournament winner Brad Faxon (151), Seve Ballesteros (155) and Ray Floyd (154).
Arnold Palmer, playing in his 43rd consecutive Masters, struggled in with an 87 after a first-round 89 for his worst ever Augusta performance.
"If I keep scoring like this, I'll take it private," said the 67-year-old Palmer, who is struggling to regain his game and his strength since having prostate cancer surgery in January.
"I won't quit playing, but I'll pick my spots to show it," added Palmer, the winner of four Masters, two British Opens and a U.S. Open.
